engine: A variation of the day<->night canon (window.DayNight). It drives the canon's reveal:'portal' — the night layer's clip-path is circle(t*145% at portalOrigin) — and turns it into a hands-on moment: the evening blooms outward in a growing circle from the exact point the visitor taps. A pulsing hotspot over a lit window invites the first touch and fades after use. To re-centre the portal per tap it re-creates the canon with the new portalOrigin (cheap destroy+create, one frame-matched pair), carrying the current t across so there is no jump, then tweens t to the opposite state.
entry: DayNightPortalReveal.create(target, { dayMedia, nightMedia, origin?, duration?, hotspot?, labels? }) -> { root, dn, bloomAt(xPct,yPct), reset, get(), destroy }. bloomAt(x,y) re-centres the portal and blooms the OPPOSITE state in; reset() blooms the day back from the default origin. The canon is driven with mode:'manual', reveal:'portal'.

seed.move: canon reveal:'portal' -> night clip-path: circle(t*145% at portalOrigin); on tap, set portalOrigin to the tapped point (% of stage) and tween t 0..1 so the evening circle grows from there. The canon reads opt.portalOrigin at apply() time, so retargeting = re-create the canon at the new origin (carry t across) then bloom.

mapping.circle_t145pct: the canon paints clip-path circle(t*145% at origin); 145% guarantees the growing circle covers the whole frame at t=1 from any corner origin.
mapping.retarget_origin: the canon reads opt.portalOrigin at apply() time and does not expose a setter, so per-tap retargeting = destroy+create at the new origin (one pair, cheap) carrying t across via dn.set(t) (no visible jump).
mapping.tap_to_pct: the tapped clientX/clientY map to (x%,y%) of the stage rect, clamped 0..100, and become the new portalOrigin; the bloom tweens t to the OPPOSITE of the current state.
mapping.bloom_tween: gsap.to(t, duration, power2.inOut) if present, else a built-in rAF lerp (factor 0.10) — both call dn.set(t) PURE.
